decisions.executionNote: Begin left-arm elbow-up approach toward the visible mallet; right arm remains parked. Raise and progressively orient before descending.
Align the open left gripper with the mallet shaft near its lower end, staying above the table and preserving elbow-up continuity.
Finish downward alignment and lower the open gripper toward the handle. Use wrist view to confirm centering before closure.
Correct small lateral and yaw offset of the shaft in the wrist image, descend the final few millimeters, and start closing around it.
Center the shaft between the fingers, fully close, then lift 36 mm to test visible retention before transporting.
Mallet is visibly retained. Raise to travel clearance and carry its head toward the leftmost red key while keeping the gripper closed.
Align the mallet head with the center of the leftmost red key, then make a controlled vertical approach for the first strike.
Finish the first red-key downstroke and lift the mallet 48 mm vertically before advancing to the next key.
Advance one key to the orange bar while raised; strike vertically and lift 50 mm afterward, keeping the mallet clamped.
Add clearance after orange, move to the third yellow bar, strike downward, then raise 66 mm to ensure separation.
Move above the fourth green key, strike it, and lift 72 mm. Keep both elbows in their current up configuration.
Lift away from green and prepare a center handoff without crossing arms. Left rotates the retained mallet upward; right rises in its own workspace with open fingers.
Continue upright mallet presentation while bringing the open right gripper toward the central handoff, leaving separation until alignment is visible.
Finish presenting the shaft vertically. Align the open right fingers about 4 cm above the left grasp, with each arm remaining on its own side.
Replan from the interrupted pose with smaller rotations to respect joint continuity, completing the upright presentation and right-hand alignment.
The upright shaft is visible inside the right opening. Make a small centering correction and close the right fingers while the left still supports the mallet.
Release the left grasp while keeping the right closed, then gently separate the hands and lift with the right to verify transfer visually.
Transfer is visibly retained by the right hand. Withdraw the open left arm and gradually rotate the mallet into a raised playing pose over the remaining keys.
Replan the unexecuted motion with half-size right wrist increments to respect IK continuity; withdraw the left arm while the right retains the mallet.
Park the open left hand farther back. Continue a gradual right-hand rotation toward a downward gripper pose, keeping the mallet above the keys.
Hold the left arm at its safe parked pose after the continuity interruption. Continue right-arm orientation above the fifth light-blue key.
Finish downward orientation and approach the fifth light-blue key vertically, pausing for a visual alignment check before the final downstroke.
Center the mallet over the fifth light-blue bar, complete its downstroke, then lift 50 mm before moving right.
Raise clear of the fifth key, move to the sixth dark-blue bar, strike downward, and lift 56 mm without changing the grasp.
Advance to the seventh purple bar at clearance, strike it vertically, then lift 56 mm while retaining the mallet.
Advance to the rightmost magenta key, strike downward, and lift the mallet 58 mm after the final hit.
